summary: Rorask Pictures Holdings, LLC (client, buyer) bought the independent film library and distribution business of Travuth Films, Inc. (seller) under an Asset Purchase Agreement. The APA was signed and closed on April 30, 2026, for $18,400,000. The folder holds: the January 2026 letter of intent; the APA; the Transition Services Agreement signed at closing, under which Travuth keeps servicing sub-distribution deals and collecting receipts; a confirmatory IP assignment dated June 15, 2026; a mutual NDA from diligence; and a laboratory access letter for the film elements. The issues all come from reading documents together. The APA's precedence clause lets each ancillary agreement control its own subject matter. That lets the TSA cut back the APA's broad 'Library Receipts' definition and apply California law and a Los Angeles forum. The TSA indemnity is said to be subject to the APA's Article IX limits, but the APA cap reaches only representation claims, so the TSA indemnity is uncapped. A Northfold streaming output license listed in the IP assignment needs consent that the APA never requires. Rorask's Title Defect Notice came after the APA's 10-Business-Day window. The APA's 12-month survival period ends before Travuth's deferred delivery deadline.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: Two documents define 'Library Receipts' differently. APA Section 1.1 defines it broadly: all receipts from exploiting the Library Films after the Effective Time, under any Contract. APA Section 6.7 says Seller will collect and remit Library Receipts only 'pursuant to the terms of' the TSA. APA Section 10.10 lets each Ancillary Agreement control as to its own subject matter. TSA Section 1.1 defines 'Library Receipts' as receipts under 'Post-Closing Sub-Distribution Agreements' only. TSA Section 3.2 limits the remittance, monthly reporting and audit obligations to Library Receipts in that narrow sense. Read together, Travuth has no contractual duty to remit, report or allow audit of receipts it collects during the service period under pre-closing sub-distribution agreements. Those are the existing library deals and the bulk of library revenue. Rorask is left with only an ownership claim to money Travuth holds.
issues.expected_finding: Because APA Section 6.7 routes Travuth's remittance duty through the TSA and APA Section 10.10 lets the TSA control its subject matter, the TSA's narrow definition of Library Receipts leaves Travuth with no obligation to remit, report or allow audit of receipts under pre-closing sub-distribution agreements. The TSA definition should be conformed to the APA definition.
detect_terms2: controls as to its subject matter

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: Exhibit A of the IP Assignment Agreement lists the existing licenses that encumber each Library Picture. One is Travuth's Exclusive SVOD Output License with Northfold Streaming, Inc. Under it, any assignment by Licensor, 'including by change of control or by sale of all or substantially all' of Licensor's film library, requires the prior written consent of Northfold. APA Section 2.1(c) transfers all Sub-Distribution Agreements as Assigned Contracts, which sweeps in the Northfold license. However, APA Schedule 2.7 (Required Consents) omits Northfold. Seller's consent covenant in APA Section 6.3 covers only Required Consents. Neither document alone shows a gap: the APA's consent list looks complete on its face, and the IP assignment exhibit is ordinary encumbrance disclosure. Read together, the sale of the library triggered Northfold's consent right, nobody obtained the consent, and no covenant or indemnity addresses it. Northfold could treat the transfer as a breach and terminate or withhold payments on a key revenue contract.
detect_terms: by change of control or by sale of all or substantially all
issues.expected_finding: The sale of the library to Rorask triggered Northfold's consent right over the output license, but Northfold is not on the APA's Required Consents schedule and Seller has no covenant to obtain its consent. Rorask should promptly seek Northfold's consent and obtain from Travuth a post-closing covenant and a special indemnity, outside the cap, for any loss of the Northfold license.

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: Under APA Section 9.1, all non-Fundamental Representations survive until twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, which is April 30, 2027. That includes the Section 3.9 representation that Delivery Materials are complete and of exhibition quality. Under APA Section 6.6, Travuth need not deliver the Delivery Materials for the Deferred Delivery Films until fifteen (15) months after the Closing Date, which is July 30, 2027. Read together, the quality representation expires three months before the materials it covers are due. Rorask cannot practically discover defects, or bring a timely claim, for materials delivered late in the period. The Section 6.6 covenant survives but requires only delivery, not quality. The LOI contemplated an 18-month survival period.
detect_terms: twelve (12) months after the Closing Date
fifteen (15) months after the Closing Date
issues.expected_finding: The Delivery Materials representation in Section 3.9 expires on April 30, 2027, before Travuth's July 30, 2027 deadline for Deferred Delivery Films, so Rorask has no practical indemnity remedy for defective deferred deliveries. Survival for Section 3.9 should be extended to a reasonable period after final delivery, consistent with the LOI's 18 months.

issues.label: governing law mismatch
issues.description: TSA Section 11.4 provides that the TSA is governed by the laws of the State of California. It gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in the County of Los Angeles. APA Section 10.8 chooses Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery. APA Section 10.10 would normally resolve conflicts in the APA's favor, but it lets each Ancillary Agreement control as to its subject matter, so the TSA's California law and forum clause stands. Neither clause is unusual alone. Together they send intertwined disputes to different courts under different law: receipts remittance under the TSA, TSA indemnity claims that TSA Section 9.4 routes through APA Article IX, and related APA representation claims. That creates a risk of parallel litigation and inconsistent results.
detect_terms: laws of the State of California
issues.expected_finding: Because APA Section 10.10 lets the TSA control its own subject matter, the TSA's California law and exclusive Los Angeles forum override the APA's Delaware law and Court of Chancery forum for TSA disputes, splitting related claims between two forums. The TSA should be amended to adopt the APA's Delaware law and forum.
detect_terms2: controls as to its subject matter

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: APA Section 2.5(a) allows a Purchase Price reduction from the Holdback for a Library Film with a Title Defect. It applies only if Buyer delivers a Title Defect Notice within ten (10) Business Days after the Closing Date. The Closing Date was April 30, 2026 (APA preamble and Section 2.9), so the deadline was May 14, 2026. Under APA Section 2.5(c), the Holdback is otherwise released to Seller. Section 6 of the IP Assignment Agreement, dated June 15, 2026, records that Rorask's Title Defect Notice for the picture 'Lantern Season' was dated May 22, 2026. It also records that Rorask maintains the picture remains subject to the price reduction. Read together, the notice was six Business Days late. Rorask's reservation of rights preserves its position but does not extend the window. Rorask's alternative remedy is an indemnity claim under the capped Section 3.8 chain-of-title representation, which must be brought before that representation's survival period ends on April 30, 2027.
detect_terms: ten (10) Business Days after the Closing Date
issues.expected_finding: Rorask's May 22, 2026 Title Defect Notice missed the May 14, 2026 deadline under APA Section 2.5(a), so the Holdback reduction for 'Lantern Season' is at risk despite the reservation of rights in the IP Assignment. Rorask should seek Travuth's written agreement to treat the notice as timely or to hold back release of the Holdback, and should preserve an indemnity claim under Section 3.8 before April 30, 2027.

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Under TSA Section 9.2, Rorask as Recipient indemnifies Travuth against all third-party claims 'arising out of the exploitation of the Library Films' or the Services during the Service Period, except to the extent of Travuth's gross negligence or willful misconduct. TSA Section 9.4 makes such claims subject to the 'limitations on liability set forth in Article IX' of the APA, which looks protective. However, APA Section 9.5(a) applies the Cap only to claims under Section 9.2(a) and Section 9.3(a), the representation-breach buckets. It does not reach TSA claims. Read together, Rorask's TSA indemnity has no cap. It covers infringement and chain-of-title claims about the films that arise from Travuth's pre-closing defects, for which Travuth's own exposure under the APA is capped at $2,760,000. It also covers Travuth's ordinary negligence in performing the Services.
detect_terms: limitations on liability set forth in Article IX
issues.expected_finding: Because the APA Section 9.5(a) Cap reaches only representation claims under Sections 9.2(a) and 9.3(a), TSA Section 9.4's cross-reference leaves Rorask's TSA indemnity uncapped, even for claims arising from Travuth's pre-closing title defects or its negligence. The TSA indemnity should be capped, should exclude matters that are Seller representation breaches or Excluded Liabilities under the APA, and should carve out Provider negligence.
